security_audit.summary: The static command, network, filesystem, environment, and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples or normal AWS configuration. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found, but the production examples include unsafe CORS and error-disclosure guidance.

remediation.issue: Wildcard CORS appears in production-oriented examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace wildcard origins and headers with explicit allowed domains, methods, and headers.

remediation.issue: API examples return raw error messages to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Return generic client errors and keep detailed diagnostics in structured logs.

remediation.issue: Several code fences are malformed or nested incorrectly.
remediation.suggestion: Fix Markdown fences so scanners and users can distinguish examples from executable instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Production Example Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents production-ready serverless guidance, but examples use wildcard CORS and return raw error messages. Users copying these patterns could expose APIs broadly or disclose internal details.

content.value_statement: Serverless teams need consistent Lambda, API Gateway, and event patterns. This skill provides AWS-focused templates, review prompts, and operational guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Provides Lambda handler patterns for Node.js and Python with error handling.
Shows API Gateway and SAM templates for HTTP APIs and DynamoDB access.
Describes SQS event processing with batch failure handling and dead-letter queues.
Highlights cold start and deployment package tradeoffs for AWS Lambda.
Lists serverless anti-patterns and sharp edges for production reviews.
limitations: Does not deploy resources or call AWS services by itself.
Examples are partial and may need validation before production use.
Does not replace IAM, threat modeling, or architecture review.
Focuses on AWS serverless services, not multicloud platforms.

use_cases.title: Scaffold Lambda APIs
use_cases.description: Create handler structure, API Gateway routes, and DynamoDB access patterns before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Event Pipelines
use_cases.description: Check SQS processing, retry behavior, and dead-letter queue design for reliable async workloads.

use_cases.title: Validate Serverless Plans
use_cases.description: Assess cold starts, package size, timeout settings, and service boundaries before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Lambda Handler
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AWS Serverless skill to outline a Lambda handler for this request: [describe the event and response].

prompt_templates.title: Design an API Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB flow for [feature]. Include routes, data access, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review an SQS Processor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SQS to Lambda design for retries, batch failures, timeouts, and dead-letter queues: [describe design].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this serverless architecture for cold starts, IAM scope, observability, CORS, and deployment risks: [paste summary].

output_examples.input: Plan a Lambda API for creating items.
output: Recommended resources include an HTTP API, one create handler, and a DynamoDB table.
The handler should validate input, write one item, and return a consistent response.
Use least-privilege table write permissions and structured logs.

output_examples.input: Review an SQS processor for order events.
output: Use batch item failure reporting so successful messages are not retried.
Set queue visibility timeout above the function timeout.
Send repeated failures to a dead-letter queue with monitoring.

output_examples.input: Improve cold start performance for a Lambda service.
output: Move reusable clients outside the handler.
Reduce package size by removing unused dependencies.
Tune memory and timeout values using measured initialization data.

best_practices: Initialize AWS clients outside Lambda handlers when safe.
Use least-privilege IAM policies for each function.
Configure retries, dead-letter queues, and observability for async workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not copy wildcard CORS settings into production without access review.
Do not return raw exception messages to API clients.
Do not place unrelated operations in one large Lambda package.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy AWS resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You must run deployment tools yourself.

faq.question: Does it support both Node.js and Python?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Lambda handler examples for both runtimes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover API Gateway?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes HTTP API and Lambda integration patterns with SAM examples.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. You still need IAM review, data protection checks, and threat modeling.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Treat examples as starting points and harden them before release.
